title: Implement Handles consultation eject and return-with-provenance exchange
description: Build a Wheelwright/Handles feature that lets a user eject the current conversation or a bounded recent slice out for external consultation, then receive a structured return prompt with provenance rather than crude copy/paste. This creates a priced consultation exchange primitive, strengthens the value of points/trails, enables automated outside-model consultation through a web service, and creates new data-value surfaces such as spot pricing and market research vectors around consultation demand.
non_goals: Do not reduce the feature to manual copy/paste wrappers
Do not expose sensitive tracks without explicit bounded consent and provenance controls
Do not require this service for core local Wheelwright operation

must_be_sequential: 1. Define the consultation eject packet: full conversation, recent points, or bounded slice.
2. Define how the system preserves point/trail value and references the source conversation precisely.
3. Define the return packet with provenance, source model/provider, timestamps, and restoration prompt shape.
4. Define the Wheelwright web service boundary that can automate consultation exchange.
5. Define monetization surfaces: member/free exchange, spot-price equivalent value, and premium automation tiers.
6. Define trust/consent/privacy rules for exported context and returned advice.
7. Persist implementation boundaries before execution begins.

verification_requirements: Verify return packets contain provenance rather than plain pasted text
Verify bounded-scope eject is supported in addition to full conversation eject
Verify the service creates reusable value for points/trails and restoration into other agents
Verify monetization and data-value surfaces are explicit without compromising consent or trust

acceptance_tests.expected: Future implementer can tell how to eject full vs partial conversation context
Returned advice is structured as a provenance-rich restore prompt, not raw pasted chat
Consultation exchange, data value, and web-service automation are all clearly separated and monetizable

review_questions: Is the consultation exchange meaningfully better than copy/paste?
Is provenance and restoration quality strong enough to build trust?
Are monetization and data-value surfaces compelling but still privacy-aware?
implementer_review.block_reason: Cluster 1 hub infrastructure (routing table + Octo) must be operational before product/commercial layer can be implemented. website/ directory does not yet exist.

product_value_map.core_value: Consult another model or service without losing chain of custody or restoration quality.
product_value_map.wheelwright_value: Strengthens tracks, points, provenance, and cross-agent continuity.
product_value_map.market_value: Creates a new consultation exchange primitive and a measurable demand signal for what users want outside models to do.

workflow.handoff_reason: Blocked until Cluster 1 ships. Do not claim.

blocking_conditions: implementation-hub-model-routing-table-v1 must be accepted (hub owns model routing)
implementation-octo-gardener-dispatch-v1 must be accepted (hub orchestration must exist)
website/ directory and hosting infrastructure must be established before implementation begins
